description.narrative: The project contributes to the N4H outcome of reducing health risks from environmental degradation, biodiversity loss, and wildlife trade and consumption. It has four linked objectives, focused on critical control points for addressing disease spillover risk, as set out in the IPD Theory of Change(TOC):1. Reduce upstream zoonosis risk by testing equitable models to reduce snaring and livestock grazing inprotected areas in cooperation with IPLCs, thereby maintaining ecological balance and enabling safereintroductions.2. Reduce zoonosis risk associated with confiscation and rescue of trafficked animals by training andcapacitating rangers, law enforcement officials, and rescue center staff to handle stressed wildlife safely andquickly.3. Reduce upstream zoonosis risk for release of rescued animals by implementing protocols to accelerate the reintroduction of healthy animals to the wild, thereby maintaining ecological balance (rewilding).4. Support the Viet Nam One Health Partnership (OHP) with N4H policy formulation and inter-agencycoordination, thereby mainstreaming project results from objectives 1-3 into policy and planning.The project will be co-implemented by IUCN, UNDP, and the government-led multi-stakeholder Viet Nam OHP,which will provide the institutional framework for integrating N4H principles into government policy andplanning.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
